claims.claim: Xiao et al. argue the Kullback-Leibler-based regularization in RLHF carries an algorithmic bias that in extreme cases produces preference collapse.
claims.source: Xiao, Li, Xie, Getzen, Fang, Long and Su, Journal of the American Statistical Association (arXiv 2405.16455 v2)
claims.quote: this bias could lead to a phenomenon we term preference collapse

claims.claim: Xiao et al. report their preference-matching RLHF variant improved alignment with human preferences by 29% to 41% over standard RLHF on one metric.
claims.source: Xiao, Li, Xie, Getzen, Fang, Long and Su, Journal of the American Statistical Association (arXiv 2405.16455 v2)

claims.claim: janus, who coined the mode-collapse usage, later corrected the post to say text-davinci-002 was not trained with RLHF.
claims.source: janus, 'Mysteries of mode collapse', LessWrong / AI Alignment Forum, 8 November 2022, with the author's later correction note
claims.quote: text-davinci-002 was not trained with RLHF

claims.claim: janus argues that raising the sampling temperature flattens the rest of the output distribution into undifferentiated goo before it helps escape a high-confidence attractor.
claims.source: janus, 'Mysteries of mode collapse', LessWrong / AI Alignment Forum, 8 November 2022
claims.quote: will flatten the rest of the output distribution into undifferentiated goo

claims.claim: janus argues the mode collapse he observed is irreducible to an effective decrease in temperature.
claims.source: janus, 'Mysteries of mode collapse', LessWrong / AI Alignment Forum, 8 November 2022
claims.quote: is irreducible to an effective decrease in temperature

claims.claim: janus reports it is sometimes possible to avoid mode collapse using prompt engineering.

claims.quote: possible to avoid mode collapse using prompt engineering
claims.page: Section on when mode collapse occurs

claims.claim: Borji concludes from kernel-density-estimate resampling experiments that the outcomes Shumailov et al. report are a statistical phenomenon and may be unavoidable.

claims.quote: the outcomes reported are a statistical phenomenon and may be unavoidable

claims.claim: Peeperkorn et al. found temperature only weakly correlated with novelty in a narrative generation task.

claims.claim: Peeperkorn et al. conclude that raising temperature does not enable access to a larger slice of the probability distribution.

claims.quote: does not enable access to a larger slice of the probability

claims.claim: Peeperkorn et al. describe the influence of temperature on creativity as far more nuanced and weak than the creativity-parameter claim suggests.
claims.source: Peeperkorn, Kouwenhoven, Brown and Jordanous, ICCC 2024 (arXiv 2405.00492)
